items.prompt: A permutation solver builds a path of chosen values. When is a complete permutation ready to record?
constraints: The input contains n distinct values.
The path invariant permits each input value at most once.

options.text: When path length equals n.
As soon as the path contains one value.
Whenever the last value differs from the previous value.
Only when the current index is zero.

feedback.reason: A permutation is complete only after every input position or value has been assigned exactly once.

blocks.text: Completion follows from the path invariant
The path contains only input values and never contains the same value twice. Therefore a path of length n contains all n distinct input values exactly once, which is precisely a permutation.

A shorter path is only a prefix and still needs choices. Once length n is reached, copy the path to the results and return from that branch; attempting another choice would create an overlong, invalid result.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Derive completion from the result shape plus the state invariant; path length alone is sufficient here only because reuse is already forbidden.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.path_nonempty: For n > 1, a one-value path leaves input values unassigned and is only a partial permutation.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_duplicate_value: One unequal adjacent pair does not prove that all n values were selected or that no earlier value was reused.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.index_zero: An index of zero usually identifies the root or first position; it says nothing about whether all n choices have been made.

items.prompt: A combination solver chooses exactly k values. Which completion condition is correct?

options.text: Record a result when the current path contains k values.
Record a result only when the candidate start reaches n.
Record immediately after the first choice.
Record whenever the current loop has no candidates.

feedback.reason: The base case must encode the exact required output size.

blocks.text: Exact-size output means exact-size completion
The path contains the values selected so far. When its length becomes k, it satisfies the requested output size, so store a snapshot and stop expanding that branch.

Reaching the end of the candidate range is different: if the path has fewer than k values, the branch is exhausted but not complete. For k = 0, the empty path satisfies the base case immediately and yields the one empty combination.

blocks.title: Separate success from exhaustion
blocks.text: A branch with no remaining candidates succeeds only if its partial result already meets the output contract.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.start_equals_n_only: The start boundary can reach n while the path still contains fewer than k values, so exhaustion alone would record an incomplete combination.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.first_choice: For k > 1, one selected value does not meet the exact-size result contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_choices: Having no candidate left is a dead end; it is a valid completion only when the path length is already k.

items.prompt: A grid word search has matched wordIndex characters. When is success complete?

options.text: When wordIndex equals the target word length.
Whenever the path reaches a grid edge.
Only after every grid cell has been visited.
Whenever the current cell has no legal neighbor.

feedback.reason: Success is defined by consuming the entire target, not by a geometric property of the grid.

blocks.text: The target, not the board, defines success

`wordIndex` is the number of target characters already matched by the current path. Equality with the target length means every required character has been consumed in order, so the solver should return success without selecting another cell.

Grid edges, visited-cell count, and available neighbors describe the search space, not completion. A path may finish in the middle of the grid, and a dead end before the last target character is a failure.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: In sequence-matching search, completion is consumption of the entire target; container geometry only determines which next transitions are legal.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.at_grid_edge: A valid word can finish in an interior cell, and reaching an edge before matching every character is still incomplete.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.visited_all_cells: The word may use far fewer cells than the board contains; visiting unrelated cells is not part of the result contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_neighbors: No legal neighbor means failure when unmatched characters remain, not automatic success.

items.prompt: A partition solver processes a string using a start index and appends valid segments to a path. When is one full partition complete?
constraints: The path segments cover exactly the prefix [0, start), without gaps or overlap.

options.text: When start equals the string length.
When the path contains at least one segment.
Whenever the most recent segment is valid.
When the next boundary is before the end.

feedback.reason: A partition is complete only when the chosen segments cover the entire input exactly.

blocks.text: The start boundary measures covered input
The path segments cover exactly the prefix [0, start). If start equals the string length, that prefix is the whole string, so the path is a complete gap-free partition and should be recorded.

A nonempty path or one valid last segment proves only local progress. When start is still smaller than the length, an unprocessed suffix remains and the branch must choose another valid segment or fail.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: For segmentation, define state as the first uncovered position; completion occurs when that boundary reaches the exclusive input end.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.path_nonempty: The first valid segment can leave most of the string uncovered, so nonemptiness is only progress.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.segment_valid: The last segment satisfying its predicate does not prove that the path covers the remaining suffix.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.end_less_length: A next boundary before the exclusive end proves that input remains; it is the opposite of completion.

items.prompt: A collect-all solver appends the current mutable path directly to results without copying it. What defect is likely?

options.text: Later mutations can change every stored result that refers to the same path object.
Appending the path automatically removes duplicate values.
The recursion can no longer return.
The stored path is automatically sorted.

feedback.reason: A completed result must preserve a snapshot of the path at that moment.

blocks.text: Store a value snapshot, not a live path reference

Backtracking reuses one path object: after recording [1, 2], it may pop 2 and append 3 to explore [1, 3]. If results stores the object itself, both entries point to the same changing list and can end with identical or empty contents.
Copying the path at completion freezes the values required by that result while allowing the working path to keep changing. An immutable path value provides the same ownership boundary.

blocks.title: Ownership rule
blocks.text: Mutable search state belongs to the active branch; recorded output must own a stable snapshot.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.duplicate_values_removed: Appending a reference performs no value comparison or deduplication; it only stores an alias to the same object.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.recursion_stops: Aliasing corrupts stored data but does not prevent calls from returning or the search from continuing.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.path_becomes_sorted: Later append and pop operations change membership, not order by value; no sorting operation occurs.

items.prompt: A find-one solver discovers a valid complete branch. Which result action matches the contract?

options.text: Return success and propagate it through callers so the search can stop.
Always append the solution and continue exploring every branch.
Immediately erase the fact that success was found.
Restart the search from the root.

feedback.reason: A boolean existence contract permits short-circuiting on the first complete valid branch.

blocks.text: Short-circuit an existence search
At a valid leaf, return `true`. Each caller that receives `true` returns it immediately instead of exploring more siblings, because the question “does one solution exist?” has already been answered.

On a failed child, restore branch-local state and continue with the next candidate. If every candidate fails, return `false`. This keeps restoration separate from the truth value: undoing a temporary choice does not erase the discovered result.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Find-one propagates success; collect-all records a snapshot and continues. Choose control flow from the result contract.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.append_and_continue_all: Continuing after success spends work to enumerate more solutions, which the find-one contract does not request.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.undo_success: State restoration removes a temporary assignment; it does not change the fact that a valid complete branch was found.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.restart_root: Restarting repeats work after existence is already proven and cannot improve the boolean answer.

items.prompt: For a solver returning all subsets, what result should the empty input produce?

options.text: A collection containing one empty subset.
An empty collection of subsets.
An error because no choice can be made.
A subset containing a null placeholder.

feedback.reason: The empty construction is a valid completed subset when the task enumerates all subsets.

blocks.text: Zero choices can form one valid construction

A subset is any selection of input elements. For an empty input, selecting nothing is valid and is the only possible selection, so the power set is {∅} and its materialized form is a collection containing one empty subset.
The distinction matters in recursive composition: one empty result acts as an identity that larger calls can extend, while an empty result collection means there are no valid constructions to extend.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Ask whether doing nothing satisfies the construction contract; if it does, empty input contributes one empty solution.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_subsets: The empty set is a valid subset of every set, including the empty set, so the result count is one rather than zero.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.error: The absence of a choice is not invalid here; it completes the one permitted empty selection.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_null_value: Null would be an element not present in the input, while the correct subset contains no elements at all.

items.prompt: A partial assignment violates a mandatory constraint before all variables are assigned. How should that state be classified?
constraints: No assignment to a remaining variable can repair the violation.

options.text: A failure state that returns without recording a result.
A complete result because the branch cannot continue.
A result that should be recorded as a partial solution.
A signal to erase every result found so far.

feedback.reason: Completion and dead-end conditions must not be conflated.

blocks.text: Dead end and valid leaf are different terminal states
The violated mandatory constraint cannot be repaired by any remaining assignment, so every descendant would be invalid. Return from this branch without recording a result.

A valid leaf satisfies every required assignment and constraint; an impossible node fails at least one nonrepairable condition. Both stop expansion, but only the valid leaf produces success or output. Failure in one sibling does not affect results from other siblings.

blocks.title: Classify terminal outcomes
blocks.text: Before returning, decide whether the node is successful, impossible, or short-circuited by an already known answer; each has different output behavior.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.successful_completion: A branch can have no valid continuation precisely because it violates the contract; inability to continue does not prove success.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.record_partial: The result requires a complete valid assignment, and this partial state is already known to violate a mandatory constraint.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.restart_all: Backtracking isolates siblings, so one failed branch neither erases earlier solutions nor requires restarting the root.

items.prompt: Why can placing a completion check only after generating children be incorrect?

options.text: A complete state may need to be recorded before any further candidate loop runs.
Every complete state always has children.
Base cases affect only speed, never correctness.
Recursive functions cannot return before a loop.

feedback.reason: A completed path is itself a result node and may intentionally have no outgoing choices.

blocks.text: A complete state is a node, not a child

Suppose a size-k combination reaches path length k. That current call already represents the completed result. Its candidate loop may intentionally be empty, so code that records only while generating a child can return without ever storing the combination.

Check completion before expansion, record or return according to the result contract, and do not generate unrelated extra choices from a terminal node. Base-case placement therefore affects which results exist, not only speed.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Test terminal meaning on the current state before asking how to create descendants.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.children_always_empty: A completed state normally needs no children; claiming that it always has children reverses the terminal-state contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.base_cases_only_optimize: A misplaced check can omit a valid leaf or record it more than once, so it changes correctness.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.recursion_no_return: A recursive call can and should return before a loop when its current state is terminal.

items.prompt: Which conditions can be legitimate backtracking base cases? Select all that apply.

options.text: The partial state satisfies the full result contract.
The partial state cannot lead to any valid completion.
A requested find-one result has already been found.
The branch appears expensive but may still contain valid solutions.

feedback.reason: Backtracking termination can represent success, failure, or contract-driven short-circuiting.

blocks.text: Three legitimate terminal meanings

items: Complete solution: emit a snapshot, increment a count, or return success as required.
Impossible state: return failure or no contribution because no valid descendant exists.
Find-one already satisfied: propagate the known success and skip all remaining siblings.
Large-looking branch: continue unless a sound bound proves that no required solution can be inside it.

blocks.text: A base case is justified by semantic finality or proven impossibility. Estimated cost alone is not a correctness argument and cannot remove a branch that may contain a required answer.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Attach an explicit return or recording action to every terminal predicate; different predicates need not share the same outcome.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.branch_looks_large: A costly branch may contain a valid required solution, so removing it without an impossibility proof breaks completeness.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.complete_solution: The state satisfies the full output contract and must be emitted, counted, or reported as success.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.impossible_state: When no descendant can become valid, returning failure avoids useless expansion without losing an answer.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.find_one_success: Once existence is proven, the caller contract permits all remaining search to terminate immediately.

items.prompt: Which actions are required when recording a completed mutable path? Select all that apply.

options.text: Store a copy or immutable snapshot of the current path.
Do not add an unrelated extra choice merely to mark completion.
Either continue or short-circuit according to collect-all versus find-one semantics.
Clear previously recorded sibling results.

feedback.reason: Recording must preserve the completed state and obey the requested result semantics.

blocks.text: Recording and control flow are separate obligations

items: Recognize completion on the current path; no artificial sentinel choice is needed.
Freeze the path by copying it or converting it to an immutable value before later undo operations.
For collect-all, store the snapshot and continue with siblings. For find-one, return or propagate success.
Keep previously recorded sibling results because each is an independent valid output.

blocks.text: Copying protects data ownership; the result contract determines whether the search continues. Solving only one of those concerns still leaves either corrupted output or incorrect control flow.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: At a valid leaf, answer two questions independently: what stable value is recorded, and whether exploration should continue.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.clear_all_results: Each sibling can produce an independent valid answer, so a later solution does not invalidate snapshots already recorded.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.copy_path: A snapshot preserves the completed values after the mutable working path is changed by undo operations.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.avoid_extra_choice: The current state already meets the completion predicate; adding a marker would change the result shape.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.follow_result_contract: Collect-all must continue to siblings, while find-one may propagate success immediately.

items.prompt: Which empty-input outcomes can be correct depending on the stated contract? Select all that apply.

options.text: One empty construction for all-subsets or all-partitions style enumeration.
False when an empty board must match a non-empty target.
Zero valid assignments when the contract requires assigning at least one missing variable.
An error for every backtracking problem with empty input.

feedback.reason: Empty input has no universal answer across backtracking problems.

blocks.text: Derive empty input from each result contract

items: All subsets or partitions: choosing no parts can be one complete empty construction, so return a collection containing that result.
Empty board with a nonempty word: no path can consume the first required character, so return false.
No candidates with at least one required variable unassigned: no complete assignment exists, so the result collection or count is zero.
Universal error: false, because empty input is often a valid boundary handled by the normal completion or failure rule.

blocks.text: The same physical input size can therefore mean identity, impossibility, or invalid input depending on the task. The mathematical result contract must decide before code chooses a default.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Ask whether the empty state already satisfies completion, proves impossibility, or violates an explicit input precondition.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.always_error: Empty subsets and empty partitions can be valid completed constructions, so emptiness is not universally invalid.

omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.one_empty_construction: Selecting or partitioning nothing can satisfy the enumeration contract exactly once.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.false_for_nonempty_target: With no board cell, the first required target character cannot be matched.
omittedCorrectExplanationsByOptionId.zero_assignments_if_variable_required: A required unassigned variable with no candidate prevents every complete assignment.

items.prompt: Arrange the control flow for a collect-all backtracking call.
constraints: The failure predicate means a nonrepairable constraint violation, not merely that the state has no children.

elements.text: If complete, record a snapshot and return from this branch.
Recurse for each choice and restore branch state.

feedback.reason: Failure and completion are resolved before expanding nonterminal states.

blocks.text: Resolve terminal states before expansion

items: Reject a state that violates a nonrepairable constraint; it has no valid descendant.
If the remaining state is complete, append a stable snapshot and return so the leaf is recorded once.
Only a valid nonterminal state needs its legal next choices generated.
For each choice, apply it, recurse, and restore the parent state before the next sibling.

blocks.text: The failure predicate must mean actual impossibility, not merely “has no children”; otherwise it could swallow a valid complete leaf. Once terminal cases are excluded, the candidate loop handles only expandable states.

blocks.title: Invariant
blocks.text: Every candidate loop starts from a valid, incomplete parent state, and every sibling starts from the same restored parent.

items.prompt: Arrange the steps for recording a completed mutable path safely.

elements.text: Verify that the completion contract is satisfied.
Create a snapshot of the current path.
Append the snapshot to the results.
Return from the completed branch without generating extra choices.

feedback.reason: A result must be recognized, frozen, stored, and then treated as terminal.

blocks.text: Freeze the leaf before the path changes

items: Evaluate the completion predicate on the current path.
Copy the path while it still contains exactly the completed values.
Append that independent snapshot to the result collection.
Return from the terminal branch; later sibling exploration will mutate only the working path.

blocks.text: Appending before copying stores an alias, while copying after undo captures the parent rather than the leaf. Continuing to choose after exact completion can create overlong invalid candidates.

blocks.title: Ownership boundary
blocks.text: The working path remains mutable; each recorded result must become independent at the completion point.

items.prompt: Arrange the checks for a find-one grid word-search call.
constraints: wordIndex is the number of target characters already matched before the current cell is validated.
The board or visited state must be restored before the call returns, on success and failure.

elements.text: If the full target is matched, return success.
Reject out-of-bounds, mismatched, or path-reused cells.
Mark the current cell as used by this path.
Search legal neighbors, restore the cell, then return whether any neighbor succeeded.

feedback.reason: Success completion is checked before attempting another cell, while invalid current states fail before mutation.

blocks.text: Success, validation, expansion, restoration

items: If wordIndex equals the target length, return true: the previous step completed the word, so no current cell is required.
Otherwise reject an invalid coordinate, character mismatch, or cell already used by this path before mutating state.
Mark the valid current cell and recursively test the legal neighbors for the next character.
Restore the cell unconditionally, then return whether any neighbor succeeded; this preserves the board for callers on both success and failure.

blocks.text: Checking bounds before the completed-target case can incorrectly reject the successful call made just beyond the last character. Skipping restoration on success can leak mutation into the caller or input even though search short-circuits.

blocks.title: Transfer rule
blocks.text: Resolve completion first, reject invalid state before mutation, and restore every mutation before returning any branch result.

items.prompt: A collect-all solver records s solutions, each containing k values, by copying the current path at completion. Select the unavoidable result-copy work and output space.
constraints: Each completed result is stored independently.
The path copy contains k values.

feedback.reason: Materializing s independent length-k results requires copying and storing sk values.

blocks.text: Derive work and storage from output volume

items: One completed path contains k values, so copying it costs O(k).
The solver records s independent paths, so total copy work is s · O(k) = O(sk).
The result collection retains the same s · k values, so output space is O(sk).

blocks.text: This is an unavoidable output cost under the explicit materialization contract. It is separate from search-tree work, live path space O(k), and recursion depth; excluding those terms does not reduce the bytes required by the returned results.

blocks.title: Output lower bound
blocks.text: When all results are returned explicitly, analyze their count times their size before considering traversal overhead.
